MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 8, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on February 8, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on February 3, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:30 pm)
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Absent:  Mayor Bucknum

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Sachs recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened
at 6:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

City Council Minutes  1  February 8, 2022
 PUBLIC HEARING

1.  Consideration of Offered District Formation Maps Including Map E-1; Withdrawal of
  Certain Maps; Racial Gerrymandering.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs opened the Public Hearing at 6:03 p.m.

  City Attorney Bill Curley stated tonight’s meeting is the fourth Public Hearing addressing the
  districting of the City under both state and federal laws that are applicable to districting. He
  mentioned, that per City Council’s direction at the last meeting, Map E was refined by the
  CDR and met with Mr. Vela’s approval. Now referred to as Map E-1. The City Attorney gave
  the City Council the option to present all maps, or streamline the process and remove some
  maps from consideration.

  Deborah Diep, Director of CDR gave an in-depth overview of the Voting District Formation
  and presented a PowerPoint presentation reviewing all seven maps.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs shared Mayor Bucknum’s request, in her absence, for Map A be revised
  by extending the northwestern boundary of District 4 into District 5 and then making
  adjustments to the remaining Districts as needed to balance the population. She requested this
  map (Map A-1) be available for the next City Council meeting.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs proposed not to eliminate any maps due to absence of the Mayor and
  the Council concurred.

  The following Mission Viejo residents spoke in favor of Map E-1; Peggy O’Neill, Deborah
  Cunningham-Skurnik, Ed Maurer, Judy Fike, Walt Lawson, Ilene Geiger, and Jon Miller.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Referred to the City Attorney’s comments pertaining to the Brown
  Act and City Council Member addresses. She stated the FAIR Maps Act is being exploited,
  as is the legal process in order for the Council to maintain their seats. Made reference to the
  Attorney General removing Bucknum, Sachs, and Raths from office. She again mentioned the
  tile system for district terms in office, and why certain maps are not being considered due to
  the number of Council Members residing in certain districts. She concluded by stating the
  City Council and City Attorney are controlling the outcome of the election.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke in favor of Map A providing five reasons it is the most equitable
  division of the City. He concluded by stating that there is no polarized voting in Mission
  Viejo, and never has been, giving himself as an example.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Referenced the workshop he attended in January of 2018, and stated here
  we are again four years later addressing the same issue. He questioned why five 5 districts,
  and suggested why not take La Paz/Marguerite, create four districts and elect a Mayor at large.

City Council Minutes  2  February 8, 2022
   Mayor Pro Tem Sachs clarified that the question he posed at the previous City Council
  Meeting on January 25, 2022, with regards to Map E, did not indicate his favorability to this
  map. He has no favorable map to this day.

  City Attorney Bill Curley explained why the process has taken a few years. He stated that
  due to the low physical spread of Hispanic residents, a minority/majority district cannot be
  formed. As such, the plaintiff agreed with the City that districting is the least effective way
  to give a voice to Hispanic residents. In 2018, the City Council recognized that and looked
  at other options. The primary option was cumulative voting. The City Attorney stated that
  per the law; you can go to districting or quote “the court may order additional remedies”.
  The Court ordered the City to investigate, and if possible, go cumulative voting. The City
  approached the Secretary of State who responded, that creating a new voting process is a
  very complicated undertaking, and would not want to do that for just one city unless we they
  received direction from the Legislator. Therefore, last year when the public said the process
  was taking too long, the City Council decided to go ahead with districting. City Attorney
  Bill Curley brought up the issue of Racial Gerrymandering and that it is Constitutionally
  prohibited. He added that the primary directive is to match the statuary state and federal
  criteria, and not primarily focus on race in the evaluation of proposed districts. Lastly, he
  said that since 1988 the City Council has comprised of five council members, with staggered
  terms. We are more than happy to look at different options, however, that is not what this
  city has historically done.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs stated that the City considered both Cumulative and Rank Choice
  voting at the onset of the lawsuit, however, the community overwhelmingly wanted to
  maintain at large voting. He added that other cities fought the lawsuit and lost, therefore,
  Mission Viejo opted to look for other choices.

  Council Member Raths shared with the public that he knows his fellow Council members,
  and that everyone on the Council enjoys serving this community, and are not power grabbers.
  He added that he is very active it the community, and that in the past four years, he has not
  spoken to one Hispanic that feels they are discriminated against. Infact, if they were to run
  for City Council they would run on their own merit and do not need to be in a special district.
  He concluded by saying, this is all money driven by the Law firm of Shenkman & Hughes,
  who are making millions of dollars suing cities in California.

  Council Member Kelley stated that the City Council are all studying the maps presented
  before them, and referenced a difference of 52 Hispanic voters between Map E-1 – District
  1, and Map A - District 3. She recognized the support for Map E-1 as it gives a greater voice
  to the Hispanic voters, and added that Map A should also be closely looked at. Lastly, she
  said that the City Council is committed to making the best decision for the residents, and
  everyone needs to be open minded and look at the factors provided by CDR and the City
  Attorney; logical boundaries, main arterial roads, communicates of interest and school
  districts.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs closed the Public Hearing at 7:23pm.

City Council Minutes  3  February 8, 2022
   Mayor Pro Tem Sachs thanked Deborah for her assistance. He asked that before working on
  Mayor Bucknum’s request that she speak to her first, and present Map A-1 at the next Council
  Meeting.

  City Attorney Bill Curley stated the Public Hearing will continue on the February 22, 2022
  City Council Meeting at 6:05pm.

PRESENTATION

P1. School Resource Officer’s School Update

  Received update from Deputy Murphy.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ed Maurer, M.V.: Gave an update on Community Choice Energy. He listed a number of
surrounding Orange County Cities that shall enjoy CCE provided by OC Power Authority next
year, and questioned why not the City of Mission Viejo? He asked that this be placed on the agenda,
and concluded by reading a quote from Supervisor 3rd District Don Wagner.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Addressed the lawsuit recently filed naming Council Members Sachs, Raths,
and Bucknum, as defendants to explain why they are still in office after being elected for a two-
year term that ended in December 2020. He stated, that he has heard, that all three are being
represented by Attorney William Curley, and questioned this representation. Lastly, he said the
residents of Mission Viejo are due an explanation.

Megan Cable, M.V.: Spoke of her opposition to the Garden Plaza Project. She mentioned she has
many concerns; however, her focus is on the mixed-use zone class, that she said does not exist in
the city at this time. She would like to see authorization of this zone, or any new zones, be set
before the citizens as a ballot measure.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Mentioned he is part of a “Stop the Monster” campaign, the Garden Plaza
project and ValueRock Realty Group. He voiced his concerns pertaining to the proposed 5 story
apartment building above a parking structure and the horrific traffic, noise, air quality
accompanying it. He mentioned numerous committees of action and a petition with 2,832
signatures to save Mission Viejo. Lastly, he asked the City Council to do the right thing and stop
the Garden Plaza.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke of his concerns to the Garden Plaza Project. He lives close by and is
concerned his view will be taken away, and questioned the traffic issues at La Paz/Marguerite. He
asked that the City share with the community what is transpiring, develop a plan, and enact a
moratorium on development.

15. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Receive report from Chief Capobianco.

City Council Minutes  6  February 8, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he was recently appointed by OCTA Chairman Mark
Murphy to represent OCTA on SCAG’s (Southern California Association of Governments)
Regional Board and Transportation Committee. He stated that Mayor Bucknum, Council Member
Kelley, and Raths also represent various committees, totaling four members of this City Council
representing South Orange County and Mission Viejo on SCAG. He added, that he also attends the
Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) Executive Committee and Board of Directors
meetings, making no shortage of zoom calls of late, as he just attended the first of these committee
meetings, which are long but informative and very important. Council Member Goodell concluded
by sharing that he participated in the Gnome Hunt & S'mores event at the Oso Creek Golf Course,
which was a lot of fun and added that the course is looking great!

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley informed everyone that the date of the Relay for Life event has moved
from April 2 to June 11, and encouraged all to view their website. She highlighted the City’s
Character word of the month program, stating that Mission Viejo established itself as a City of
Character in 2003. The Character Program focuses on a different word each month and as such,
materials are provided to each of the twenty-six schools in Mission Viejo. She stated the word for
February is Unity and proceeded to read a couple of quotes. The first from Coach Paul Bear Bryant
“In order to have a winner, the team must have a feeling of unity. Every player must put the team
first ahead of personal glory”, and the second quote, she feels is exemplified by this City Council
is from Mother Teresa “I can do things you cannot, you can do things I cannot. Together we can do
great things”.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked everyone in the audience for their participation in this evenings
meeting, adding that involvement in one’s community is very important. He stated that he is a big
supporter of the Chamber of Commerce, and attends their weekly meetings every Tuesday morning
at 8am at the Norman P. Murray Center. Lastly, together with Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, and Council
Member Goodell, he attended the 100th birthday celebration of Captain Leland Spencer this past
Saturday, February 5, a B24 Bomber Pilot with the Eighth Airforce in Europe. Happy Birthday
Leland!

City Council Minutes  7  February 8, 2022
 Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs addressed the comment made earlier pertaining to Community Choice
Energy. He stated the City has been paying close attention to what is going on, and there are several
reasons why the City is not, at this time, entering into an agreement with JPA (Joint Powers
Authority). He himself, is opposed to this idea, as the City of Irvine has two seats on the board
while all other cities only have one member. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs further stated that Utility
companies are charging more money to join the grid, and CPUC (California Public Utilities
Commission) are wanting to charge a huge fee to those who have solar power to help offset the cost
of those who do not. Lastly, he said that right now it is not in the best interest of the residents of
Mission Viejo to joining the CCE Operation.

At the hour of 8:16 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 22, 2022, at 5:00 p.m.
